chunks: Ali, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abu Ja'far Al-Sa'igh, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and Abu Hanifa was with him. So I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, I saw a strange dream.' He said to me, 'O Ibn Muslim, bring it forth, for the one knowledgeable about it is seated here,' and he gestured with his hand to Abu Hanifa. I said, 'I saw as if I had entered my house, and my family had come out at me, breaking many walnuts and scattering them upon me. So I was astonished by this dream.' Abu Hanifa said, 'You are a man who disputes and argues bitterly regarding the inheritance of your family, so after great hardship you will attain your need from it, if Allah wills.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'You have hit it, by Allah, O Abu Hanifa.'

He said, 'Then Abu Hanifa left from his presence, so I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, I disliked the interpretation of this Hostile One (Nasibi).' He said, 'O Ibn Muslim, may Allah not displease you. Their interpretation does not match our interpretation, nor does our interpretation match theirs, and the interpretation is not as he has interpreted it.' I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, you said 'you hit it' and swore upon it, while he was mistaken.' He said, 'Yes, I swore that he hit the mistake.'

I said to him, 'So what is its interpretation?' He said, 'O Ibn Muslim, you will do Mut'ah with a woman, and your family will learn of it, so she will tear up new clothes for you, for the shell is the clothing of the nut.'

Ibn Muslim said, 'By Allah, there was not a Friday between his interpretation and the verification of the dream. So when it was the morning of the Friday, I was sitting at the door when a maid passed by me who pleased me. So I ordered my slave to bring her back, then I brought her into my house and I enjoyed her. My family sensed it and they came into the house. The maid hastened towards the door and I remained, so she tore up new clothes for me which I used to wear during the Eids.'

And Musa Al-Zawwar the perfumer came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, I saw a dream that alarmed me. I saw my brother-in-law who was dead embracing me, and I feared that the term (of death) had drawn near.' He said, 'O Musa, expect death morning and evening, for it will meet us. And the embracing of the dead by the living is longevity for their lives.' He said, 'What is the name of your brother-in-law?' He said, 'Husayn.' He said, 'Indeed, your dream indicates your remaining alive and your visiting Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), for everyone who is embraced by one named Husayn will visit him, if Allah wills.'

key_terms.النَّاصِبِ: The Hostile One (referring to Abu Hanifa in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of seeing a dead person named Husayn embracing you in a dream according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the distinct epistemological authority of the Imams in dream interpretation, contrasting Imam Al-Sadiq’s precise insight with the scholarly intuition of Abu Hanifa, who was deemed a 'Nasibi' (rival) yet accurate in his specific case. The narrative underscores the Shia view that while non-Shia scholars may occasionally hit the mark, their interpretive framework differs fundamentally from the Ahl al-Bayt, as illustrated by the correction regarding the tearing of clothes and the symbolic meaning of embracing a namesake of Husayn.
